newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks end lower ahead of bank holiday.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks end lower ahead of bank holiday.

text.p: Croatian stocks ended lower across the board on Thursday after trade slowed down ahead of the long weekend which starts with a bank holiday on Friday.
Of 14 active shares 10 fell, two rose and two were flat.
Traders blamed the fall of prices and slower trade on the lack of investors, but disagreed over whether this pointed to a downward trend or was just a temporary correction.

"It is obvious that the summer has begun today. Last year it began on July 15, this year a little bit later," said Velimir Zelimorski of Fima brokerage, adding that most market participants chose mid-August to take their summer holidays.
Weekly turnover shrank to 28.7 million from 36.3.
"All stock prices went down, but it is too early to say whether it is the beginning of a downward trend or just a temporary correction. We'll have to wait till next week to see," Zelimorski said.

Marijana Reskovac of Karlovacka Banka brokerage also blamed the accute shortage of market participants for the slower activity, but said the market would recover as soon as they returned from the long weekend.
"I believe that the market will recover. As soon as we are all back and the normal competition is restored, the prices will go up again," Reskovac said.

Turnover fell to 5.3 from 7.4 million kuna, of which 0.9 million accounted for government bonds. Volume rose to 15,804 from 11,171 shares, mostly thanks to one issue that accounted for two thirds of the trade.

Dubrovnik-based shipper Atlantska Plovidba which rarely trades was by far the most active issue, selling 10,129 shares in what traders said seemed to be a pre-arranged deal. It lost 10 kuna from July 18, when it last traded, to close at 150.
Other stocks traded in meagre volumes except for brewery Karlovacka Pivovara and food processor Podravka.
Podravka was the top decliner, closing 18 kuna or 6.9 percent down at 262, after dipping as low as 250 kuna on volume of 2,376 shares.

Reskovac said small shareholders, who were the most active in offering their stakes in Podravka in recent weeks, tend to be "impatient", selling shares when they start going down and thus only accelerating their fall.
But it is unlikely Podravka would go further down, she said. "I think its realistic price is closer to around 300 kuna than what it is at the moment."

Karlovacka Pivovara was the one of just two issues to resist the trend, adding 10 kuna to 660 on volume of 1,768 shares. The other was Koncar electrical concern, which rose 50 kuna to 1,250, but only five shares changed hands.
